REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFItæ OF THE UNDERSEQETARY FOR LOCAL 8 22 s. 200 14 April 2008 HON. WALFREDO A. SUMILANG 11 Sangguniang Panlungsod Member Tayabas City, Quezon Dear Sir: This pertains to your letter requesting for the Department's legal opinion regarding the appointments issued by the President of the Republic of the Philippines to you and to Ms. Tomasa N. Llaneta as Sangguniang Panlungsod Members of that city. In your letter, you stated that the Municipality of Tayabas was converted into a component city and for such conversion, a plebiscite was held on 14 July 2007 where said conversion was ratified by the people. The municipality had eight (8) regular Members of the Sangguniang Bayan. However, in view of its conversion duly ratified in a plebiscite, there is a need for two (2) more Members to complete the new set of the Sangguniang Panlungsod which under RA 6636, is fixed by law to be with ten (10) regular Sangguniang Panlungsod Members for component cities. After receipt of the appointments issued by the President to complete the new set of the Sangguniang Panlungsod, you and Ms. Llaneta immediately took your oath of office and assumed as Sangguniang Panlungsod Members. In the 03 March 2008 session of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Tayabas City, City Vice Mayor Venerando Rea, however, refused to recognize you and Ms. Llaneta as the new Sangguniang Panlungsod Members despite the presentation of your credentials, i.e. appointments papers and oath of office. As a result, you and Ms. Llaneta were prevented from participating in the then on- going deliberation of the Sangguniang Panlungsod. Your query are now on the following issues: 1. "Does City Vice Mayor Venerando Rea has the power to deny recognition of the appointments made by the President of the Philippines in accordance with the provisions of Republic Act No. 6636?

-2- 2. Does the City Vice Mayor possess the power to prevent the two (2) additional duly appointed members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod ng Tayabas from participating in the deliberation of the council? If not, can he be held accountable for this act? 3. If the two (2) newly appointed member of the SP of Tayabas are to be recognized, when are they considered to have assumed their official functions?" In reply to your first query, it is settled in our jurisprudence that actions made by public officials enjoy the presumption of legality and validity until such time declared otherwise by a competent court. At this point, may we note that the President issued said appointments in furtherance of her residual powers under Section 16, Article VII of the 1987 Constitution in relation to RA 6636 which mandates that for component cities, there shall be ten (10) regular members of the Sanggunian. In view of the insufficiency of the number of regular members of the then Sangguniang Bayan, the President exercised her constitutional authority to issue the two (2) appointments. Therefore, it is not within the prerogative of the City Vice Mayor to recognize or not said appointments. It is not also the prerogative of the City Vice Mayor to exercise discretion whether to allow you and Ms. Llaneta or not to participate in the Sanggunian sessions since having been appointed as SP Members, your membership to the Sangguniang Panlungsod shall be by operation of law, the President having issued said appointments pursuant to her residual authority under the Constitution. Stated differently, your membership to the Sangguniang Panlungsod is not determined through the recognition or non-recognition by the City Vice Mayor as in fact legally saying, you and Ms. Llaneta are now considered Sangguniang Panlungsod Members by virtue of the appointments issued by the President. The City Vice Mayor should be reminded of the rule of law such that the appointments having been duly issued by the President and their authenticity having been already verified, he cannot just unilaterally disregard the same but instead, he should accord due respect to it, owing to the authority who issued the said appointments. If he believes that the appointments may have suffered from certain legal infirmities, his remedy is not to prevent you from participating in the Sanggunian sessions or not recognizing you as Sangguniang Panlungsod Members but by taking the legal steps, he should go to court and bring to fore the legality or illegality of the said appointments. Meantime, there being no declaration from any court on the state of said appointments, the same should be given legal force and effect. In reply to your second query, may we note that our reply to your first issue has already answered portions thereof. In addition, Section 3 (e) of RA 3019 is

-3- instructive in providing that any public officer who caused undue injury to another shall be criminally liable. At this point, it bears to note that the continued non- recognition as SB Members and the refusal of the City Vice Mayor to allow you and Ms. Llaneta to participate in the sessions of the Sanggunian as the new regular Sangguniang Panlungsod Members will undoubtedly cause undue injury to both of you. This unjustifiable refusal will further give rise to a possible administrative case of abuse of authority. In reply to your third query, generally, the operative act that would signify one's assumption to public office is the taking of his oath and the actual assumption and discharge of the powers and functions pertaining to the said office. At this point, may we note that while you have already taken your respective oaths of office, you were unable, however, to discharge the functions of the office due to the refusal of the City Vice Mayor to recognize. Be that as it may, we are of the considered view that from the time you have taken your oath of office and from the time that you were willing and able to already perform and discharge the functions of your office, if not for the refusal of the City Vice Mayor, you and Ms. Llaneta are already considered to have assumed the office and thus, entitled to the benefits thereof. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADE O IJndersecretary Legal:43/La cc: Director Roberto C. Abejero DILG Regional Office No. IV-A FTI Complex, Taguig City
